title: The roof of the Grimstad hall
bodyMd: Visitors to the medieval guild hall at Grimstad often admire its roof, whose oak beams span nearly twenty meters without a single supporting column. Guidebooks credit the design to Master Håkon, the carpenter named in the hall's founding charter of 1374. Yet when conservator Liv Aasen dated the beams by their growth rings, she found that the trees had been felled in the 1560s, nearly two centuries after the charter was written. The assembly marks cut into the timbers, moreover, match those of a carpentry workshop known to have operated only in that later period. The roof that visitors admire, Aasen concludes, is a sixteenth-century replacement, not Master Håkon's work.

The assembly marks cut into the timbers also match those of a carpentry workshop known to have operated only in that later period. Aasen concludes that the roof is a sixteenth-century replacement, not Master Håkon's work.
